metadata.description: Board 1: Workflow Architecture — actual and documented certification workflow for the CMA Part 1 Exam Simulator
metadata.precedes: S200 found 72 agents, 8 gates + 6 boards, 89.5% readiness failure rate, 8 duplicate review categories

executive_summary.critical_gap: The documented CAQS 7-step sequential pipeline (Accountant → Editor → Psychometrician → Validator → Release Manager) has NEVER been executed as designed. Actual certification uses parallel 10+ agent boards with duplicated review categories. 89.5% of items arrive at boards with 3-5 concurrent defects, requiring 2-3 additional remediation sessions per wave.

system_1_documented_content_quality.label: CAQS §8-§9 Documented Quality Gates (G1-G7)
system_1_documented_content_quality.description: Sequential 7-gate pipeline from content creation to production release. Each gate requires a minimum rubric score and a specific persona reviewer.

gates.name: Technical Review
entry_criteria: Question has complete stem, choices, and metadata
Assigned to a sub-batch for review
exit_criteria: Accounting accuracy verified against GAAP/COSO/IMA standards
Standard references correctly cited (ASC, IFRS, COSO)
dependencies: Item must exist in a pack file with QuestionID
automated_checks: EV3 — Correct answer explanation references accounting principle by name
DL-009 — ASC citation cross-check against known-good topic→standard mapping
DL-030 — CorrectChoice vs independently derived answer
human_decisions: Is the accounting treatment correct under current standards?
Does the formula correctly test the intended concept?
Are standard references precise enough (e.g., ASC 450-20-25 not just ASC 450)?
failure_modes: Accounting error → rejected without further scoring
Missing or wrong standard citation
Formula does not match question stem data

gates.name: Psychometric Review
exit_criteria: Difficulty assignment verified against CAQS §6.1 targets
Distractor quality evaluated (plausibility, distinctness, trap coverage)
dependencies: G1_DOC — Technical Review must PASS first
automated_checks: DL-005 — Distractor similarity (Jaccard > 70% between distractor pairs)
Answer pattern analysis — no runs > 4 same position
human_decisions: Is the difficulty label appropriate for the cognitive demand?
Do distractors represent documented exam traps?
Is the question free of cueing and bias?
Does the question genuinely test at the assigned Bloom's level?
failure_modes: Difficulty inflation (Moderate labeled for Remember/Understand items — DL-031)
Uniform difficulty across entire case bank (DL-032)
Overlapping distractors testing same misconception
Grammatical or length cueing pointing to correct answer

gates.name: Numerical Validation
exit_criteria: Independent recalculation matches stored Correct value
dependencies: G2_DOC — Psychometric Review must PASS first
automated_checks: EV5 — Formula numbers in explanation match exhibit values
EV6 — Arithmetic result in explanation matches Correct value
human_decisions: Is the formula correct for the concept being tested?
Was the reviewer truly independent (did not see stored answer)?
Are non-cash items treated correctly?
failure_modes: Numerical error → auto-fail, rejected without further scoring
Independent answer disagrees with stored Correct value
Rounding applied at wrong step
Time period mismatch (annual vs. monthly)

gates.name: Instructional Review
entry_criteria: G3 Numerical Validation PASS (or CalculationRequired: false)
exit_criteria: Explanation complies with CAQS §4 (all required elements present)
Writing clarity and professional tone verified
dependencies: G3_DOC — Numerical Validation must PASS first
automated_checks: EV1 — Minimum 50 characters per explanation field
human_decisions: Does the explanation function as a mini-lesson?
Is the business interpretation meaningful in context?
Are distractor explanations genuinely educational?
Does the explanation identify a specific exam trap?
failure_modes: Generic distractor explanations (DL-013 boilerplate)
Missing accounting principle reference (EV3)
Explanation describes wrong choice (DL-010)
One-sentence explanation for Apply/Analyze/Evaluate items (G-NEW-4)

gates.name: Metadata Review
exit_criteria: All required metadata fields present (QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md Part 8)
dependencies: G4_DOC — Instructional Review must PASS first
automated_checks: CF2 — Topic within scope of BlueprintDomain
CF4 — Case difficulty within ±1 of mean item difficulty
human_decisions: Are optional but recommended fields populated?
Are formula references correct?
failure_modes: Metadata failure → rejected without further scoring
Missing required fields that would break application
Cross-reference to non-existent exhibit or formula

gates.name: Final Validation
exit_criteria: Automated validation suite passes with ZERO errors
All Gold Standard Checklist items satisfied
dependencies: G5_DOC — Metadata Review must PASS first
automated_checks: Full validation suite (all validators in scripts/validators/)
app.js test suite: 186 tests all PASS
All 13 runtime file hashes match CURRENT_BASELINES.md
human_decisions: Compare before/after metrics for regressions
Verify no unintended pack-file corruption
failure_modes: New validation errors introduced by remediation
Hash drift from concurrent sessions
QuestionID count change (items lost or duplicated)

gates.name: Approval
dependencies: G6_DOC — Final Validation must PASS first
automated_checks: All prior gate PASS records verified
human_decisions: Are all findings communicated?
Is the item ready for learner delivery?
Are exception requests documented with remediation plans?
failure_modes: Gate results self-reported without verification (violates AGENTS.md §5)
Certification without REVISION_HISTORY.md entry
ProductionStatus changed without all gates actually passing

system_2_operational_certification_gates.label: Operational Certification Gates (Gates 0-5) — As Actually Practiced
system_2_operational_certification_gates.source: REVISION_HISTORY.md patterns: S807, S808, S809, S319, S200
system_2_operational_certification_gates.status: ACTIVE — The actual gate system used in certification sessions
system_2_operational_certification_gates.description: This is the gate system that emerged organically from 14 certification sessions (S301-S809). It diverges significantly from the documented CAQS pipeline. Gates are executed in parallel by 10+ agents rather than sequentially. The system includes 6 additional review boards.

gates.name: Gate 0 — Duplicate Prevention & Registry Check
entry_criteria: QuestionIDs are assigned or batch is defined
exit_criteria: All QIDs confirmed collision-free across ALL 10 pack/case files
dependencies: Registry must be up to date
automated_checks: Select-String all pack/case files for QID presence
human_decisions: Dual-presence: is this a clone, replacement, or genuine duplicate?
Does pending replacement risk block certification?
failure_modes: Dual-presence conflict with Certified replacement items
Registry stale — QID exists but not in current index
Template rotation creates 5+ copies of same QID (variant confusion)

gates.name: Gate 1 — Draft / Content Completeness
entry_criteria: Items identified with QuestionIDs and line numbers
exit_criteria: All items confirmed present in pack file at correct line numbers
All have: stem, 4 choices, CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect, ExplanationWrong[A-D]
question_state correctly set (Unprocessed / In Audit / Certified / Archived)
human_decisions: Is question_state consistent with claimed certification status?
Is the item using single-object or dual-block architecture?
Are content-block and metadata-block choices consistent? (DL-016 check)
failure_modes: question_state missing entirely (DL-024 — 1,101 of 2,500 items pre-S18)
Wrong question_state for certification status (e.g., 'Certified' with DL-008)
Dual-block architecture with metadata-content divergence (DL-016)
Line-number targeting failure (template rotation: same QID at multiple offsets)

gates.name: Gate 2 — Technical Review / Structural EW Audit
gates.reviewer: EW Audit Agent / Technical Accuracy Agent
entry_criteria: DW (data-warehouse) Import or direct file scan completed
exit_criteria: DL-008: ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] is empty for all items
DL-010: ExplanationWrong fields describe their designated choices (not offset)
DL-013: Zero template boilerplate ('represents a plausible misconception')
DL-026: All non-CorrectChoice ExplanationWrong slots non-empty
DL-021: All distractor ExplanationWrong fields structurally present
ExplanationCorrect ≥ minimum quality threshold (per item type)
ExplanationCorrect references COSO/ASC/GAAP standard by name
All answer keys independently verified (stored CC = derived CC)
Zero accounting errors in stems or choices
automated_checks: DL-013 scan: boilerplate pattern match ('represents a plausible misconception')
DL-026 scan: empty non-CC EW slot detection
DL-021 scan: absent EW field detection
DL-010 scan: EW text vs designated choice semantic alignment
EC length check: ≥ 200 characters minimum (case items: depth-appropriate)
human_decisions: Is the EW text choice-specific or boilerplate?
Is the EW text topically relevant? (G-NEW-2 — certification BLOCK if not)
Does the EC provide sufficient depth for the cognitive level? (G-NEW-4)
Template rotation artifact: is the empty slot a CC slot or a distractor slot?
Does the dual-block architecture require within-object verification? (G-NEW-3)
failure_modes: DL-008 — non-empty EW[CC] (most common structural defect, still OPEN for 174 Pack C items)
DL-026 — empty non-CC EW slots (rotation artifact, 53 empty in Domain E seeds)
DL-013 — template boilerplate in EW fields (~851 fields remaining)
DL-016 — metadata-block shift causes EW scan false positives
DL-010 — EW text assigned to wrong choice due to rotation offset
DL-021 — missing EW fields entirely (Pack E Section C: 100 items)
G-NEW-2 — EW text topically unrelated to item (blocks certification)

gates.name: Gate 3 — Blueprint Alignment Review
exit_criteria: LOSTag mapped to precise CSO subsection (not just domain-level 'E Internal controls')
Blueprint domain coverage assessed against IMA CSO
LOS coverage gaps identified and documented
All 6 blueprint domains audited for coverage balance
human_decisions: Is the LOSTag precise enough (e.g., 'E.1.e Control Activities' not just 'E Internal controls')?
Is there over-concentration in any single LOS area?
Are LOS gaps acceptable or do they need new items?
Does the item genuinely test the claimed learning outcome?
failure_modes: Coarse LOSTags ('E Internal controls' — too generic for certification)
Over-concentration (e.g., SoD items at 21% vs. target ~8%)
LOS gaps with zero seeds (e.g., E.1.h SOX had 0 seeds)
Topic misalignment: item tests different LOS than LOSTag claims

gates.name: Gate 4 — QA Review (Cognitive Calibration + Difficulty)
gates.reviewer: CognitiveLevel Agent / Difficulty Agent / Learner Safety Agent
exit_criteria: CognitiveLevel verified against Bloom's taxonomy requirements
Difficulty and DifficultyScore consistent with CAQS §6.1 targets
DL-031: No definition-match items labeled above Easy
DL-032: Not all items uniformly labeled (zero variance detection)
Cueing and bias checks: no grammatical/length/position cues
Learner safety: no known-defective QIDs in delivery pool
automated_checks: DL-031: lexical overlap between stem and correct answer > 50% with difficulty ≥ Moderate
DL-032: difficulty label distribution (flag if single label ≥ 90%)
human_decisions: Does the cognitive level match the actual cognitive demand?
Is this a definition-match item that should be Easy (1) not Moderate (3)?
Are distractors genuinely deceptive at the claimed difficulty level?
Is the DifficultyScore consistent with the Difficulty label?
failure_modes: DL-031: Systematic difficulty inflation (~500 items estimated)
DL-032: Case bank — 100% Moderate, zero variance (420 items)
CognitiveLevel assigned by rotation position, not item content (19/38 seeds overstated)
DifficultyScore/Label mismatch (e.g., 'Easy' with DifficultyScore: 3)

gates.name: Gate 5 — Certification Candidate / Final Adjudication
entry_criteria: Non-blocking defects documented with remediation plans
exit_criteria: All HOLD items have specific remediation assignments
All CERTIFY items have question_state → 'Certified' transition authorized
QA Board: ALL_AGREE (all agent tracks convergent)
automated_checks: governance-guard.js Rule 2: EW[CC] must be empty (BLOCK)
All 13 runtime file hashes vs T0 baseline
human_decisions: Does this item meet CAQS §1.7.2 certification requirements?
Are all 6 verification dimensions at HIGH confidence?
Is user approval documented?
Are any pre-S508 items flagged for G-NEW-2/3/4 violations?
failure_modes: Items arrive with 3-5 concurrent defects (89.5% readiness failure rate)
Certification board agents disagree — no ALL_AGREE convergence
Certification without REVISION_HISTORY.md entry
question_state changed without gate authorization
Pre-S508 certified items have G-NEW violations (remain Certified but flagged)
Certified count instability between scans (violates AGENTS.md §6)
Totals-only reports without QID lists accepted (violates AGENTS.md §5)

boards.name: Readiness Board
boards.function: Pre-board scoring and classification. Rates items as READY / MINOR_FIX / HOLD / ESCALATE based on defect inventory and remediation effort. Assigns waves (A/B/C/D) and batches.
boards.agents: Scoring Agent, Batch Planning Agent, Readiness Assessment Agent

boards.name: QA Board
boards.function: Convergence verification. Checks that all agent tracks independently agree on item status, defects, and recommendations. Flags dissenting opinions. Validates ALL_AGREE status.

boards.name: Certification Board
boards.function: Final adjudication. Issues CERTIFY / HOLD / ESCALATE verdicts. Authorizes question_state transitions. Requires ALL_AGREE from QA Board.
boards.agents: Certification Agent, Portfolio Impact Agent, Forecast Agent

boards.name: Governance Board
boards.function: Runtime governance verification. Hash audits, CAPA checks, certified denominator reconciliation, governance-guard compliance.
boards.agents: Startup Governance Agent, Baseline & CAPA Auditor, Ledger Reconciliation Agent

boards.name: Closure Board
boards.function: End-of-session governance closeout. REVISION_HISTORY.md write, governance guard re-verification, certified count confirmation, Tend hash audit.

boards.name: Learner Safety Board
boards.function: Pre-delivery safety check. Confirms delivery pool only pulls 'Certified' items. Cross-references known-defective QID list. Flags any defective QID still in delivery pool.

system_4_certification_blocking_rules.label: G-NEW Certification Blocking Rules (Session 508, 2026-07-25)
system_4_certification_blocking_rules.status: ACTIVE — effective 2026-07-25. Pre-existing certified items grandfathered but flagged.
system_4_certification_blocking_rules.description: Additional certification-blocking conditions discovered during Session 700 global certification review. These close governance gaps where structurally non-empty but semantically wrong ExplanationWrong fields passed certification.

rules.name: Learner-Facing Choice Authority
rules.description: Content-block Choices.{A,B,C,D} are authoritative. Metadata-block ChoiceA-D may not override learner-facing content when a conflict exists.
rules.verification: Compare metadata-block ChoiceA-D vs content-block Choices.{A,B,C,D}. If differ → BLOCK.

rules.name: Explanation Relevance Certification Block
rules.description: Any EW field with text belonging to a different question, different topic, different template instance, or otherwise semantically unrelated to the learner-facing distractor → certification BLOCKED.
rules.verification: Semantic relevance check: does EW text describe this item's actual choices? Non-empty ≠ sufficient.

rules.name: Dual-Block Verification Requirement
rules.description: CorrectChoice must be extracted from the same enclosing JSON object as the EW fields being evaluated. Forward-scan or regex-window scanning is NOT sufficient.
rules.blocked_by: DL-029 scan methodology defects, DL-016 offset in dual-block packs
rules.verification: Within-object CC extraction (Function constructor parse or brace-matched JSON). Packs A/C/D require this.

rules.name: Case Explanation Minimum Standard
rules.description: One-sentence explanations for Apply/Analyze/Evaluate items blocked. Select/multi/match items without distractor rationale blocked. Missing authoritative standard citation blocked.
rules.blocked_by: Insufficient explanation depth, missing COSO/ASC/G AAP citations
rules.verification: EC length < 200 chars for Apply+ items, missing standard citation, no distractor guidance.

rules.name: Updated Certification Checklist
rules.description: 5 new certification gate checks: G5.1 (topic relevance), G5.2 (source-of-truth for dual-block), G5.3 (case explanation sufficiency), G5.4 (case distractor rationale), G5.5 (authoritative standard citation).

critical_gaps.title: Documented Sequential Pipeline vs. Actual Parallel Board Execution
critical_gaps.description: CAQS §9.1 documents a sequential 7-step pipeline where each gate must PASS before the next begins (Accountant → Editor → Psychometrician → Validator → Release Manager). The actual system uses 10+ parallel agents across 6 boards with no sequential dependency. This means the documented authority matrix (COLLABORATION_MATRIX.md) is never exercised — Accountant does not review before Editor, Psychometrician does not wait for Accountant.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Either update CAQS to reflect actual parallel board architecture, or redesign the actual workflow to enforce documented sequential review.

critical_gaps.title: No Pre-Board Structural Scan — 100% Domain E Readiness Failure
critical_gaps.description: 38 Domain E seeds reached S809 certification with zero pre-board structural scans. Every single one was blocked at Gate 2 (53 empty EW slots, 8 DL-013 boilerplate slots). No automated detection ran before the certification board was assembled. All 38 items had known DL-026 and DL-016 defects that could have been detected by automated pre-flight scans.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Add mandatory automated pre-flight scans (DL-008, DL-013, DL-026, DL-016, DL-010, DL-021, DL-031) BEFORE any certification board convenes. Items that fail pre-flights should not enter Gate 2.

critical_gaps.title: EW Field Duplicate Review — 4-7 Agents Re-Examine Same Fields
critical_gaps.description: S200 found 8 duplicate review categories, with ExplanationWrong fields being the worst case: 4-7 separate agents independently re-examine the same EW fields per session. Each agent produces a separate report — many of which are never consumed (65% one-off rate). This is the primary driver of the 1,212 report bloat.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Consolidate EW field auditing into a single agent pass with comprehensive output. Eliminate redundant re-examination. Implement delta review: only re-audit items that changed between sessions.

critical_gaps.title: No Delta Review — 80% Unchanged Items Re-Audited Every Session
critical_gaps.description: S200 found that 80% of items are unchanged between certification waves, yet all items are re-audited from scratch each session. The Certification Framework v2 proposes SHA-256 content hashes for delta inheritance. Implementing delta review could save ~77% of time per session.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Implement per-item SHA-256 content hashing. Store hashes in a delta ledger. Only re-audit items whose hash changed from the last certification wave.

critical_gaps.title: Dual-Block Architecture vs. Scan Tools — Persistent False Positives
critical_gaps.description: Packs A, C, and D use dual-block architecture (metadata block + content block). Scan tools that use forward-scan or regex-window methodology (not within-object CC extraction) systematically produce false positives. Session 501 found 39 Pack D Section C items falsely flagged as DL-008/DL-026 due to cross-object CC reading. Pack B DL-008 was falsely counted at 111 (actual: 0) due to CC-before-QuestionID object ordering.
critical_gaps.recommendation: All scan tools must use within-object extraction (Function constructor parse or string-aware brace-matching). Totals-only reports without QID lists must be rejected per AGENTS.md §5. Forward-scan/regex-window methodology must be deprecated.

critical_gaps.title: 89.5% Readiness Failure Rate — Items Arrive at Boards with 3-5 Defects
critical_gaps.description: The fundamental certification workflow problem: items reach the certification board in a state that guarantees they will be blocked. Each item carries 3-5 concurrent defects (typically DL-026 empty EW slots + DL-013 boilerplate + DL-016 offset + DL-031 difficulty inflation). Remediation then requires 2-3 additional sessions (S320-S325 pattern). The certification board becomes a defect-discovery session, not an approval session.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Implement a 'pre-board readiness gate' that runs automated defect scans before items enter the certification pipeline. Items must achieve 'pre-board ready' status (all known defect categories scanned, all blocking defects resolved) before entering Gate 0.

critical_gaps.title: Case Study Items: Zero Difficulty Calibration (DL-032)
critical_gaps.description: All 420 case items across 75 cases are labeled Difficulty: 'Moderate'. Zero are Easy, Difficult, or Very Difficult. This is statistically impossible for a real exam pool. The documented CAQS §9.2 review process was never applied to case items — they were generated with template defaults and never calibrated.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Recalibrate all 420 case items using the CAQS §6.1 target distribution (Easy 15%, Moderate 30%, Difficult 25%, Very Difficult 10%).

critical_gaps.title: CAQS G3 Numerical Validation Never Executed as Separate Gate
critical_gaps.description: The documented G3 (Numerical Validation by Validator — independent recalculation) has never been observed in actual certification sessions. Numerical validation is subsumed into Gate 2 (Technical Review) where the Technical Accuracy Agent verifies stored CorrectChoice = independently derived answer. The formal independent recalculation pipeline (solve blind → compare → reconcile) from CAQS §5.1 is not followed.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Either fold G3 into Gate 2 officially, or formalize the blind independent recalculation as a distinct step.

critical_gaps.title: No Release Manager Role in Practice
critical_gaps.description: The documented G7 gate (Approval by Release Manager — final sign-off for production) does not exist in the actual workflow. Certification decisions are made by the Certification Board (convergent multi-agent adjudication). The Release Manager persona from COLLABORATION_MATRIX.md has no operational equivalent in observed sessions.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Either retire the Release Manager role from documentation, or instantiate it as the final adjudication step after Certification Board convergence.

critical_gaps.title: Reporting Bloat: 65% of 1,212 Reports Never Consumed
critical_gaps.description: The report generation pattern has grown from 2.7 files/session (early) to 11.7 files/session (recent). 829 JSON reports and 371 markdown reports exist. 65% are one-off artifacts that are never referenced again. S200 Certification Framework v2 proposes 4 reports/session.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Standardize to 4 reports per session (Session Summary, Certification Results, Defect Ledger Update, Handoff Manifest). Eliminate per-agent one-off reports.

critical_gaps.title: Session 508 G-NEW Rules Not Integrated Into Gate Automation
critical_gaps.description: The G-NEW-1 through G-NEW-5 rules (effective 2026-07-25) add critical certification-blocking conditions but have not been integrated into automated gate checks. G-NEW-2 (topic relevance) requires semantic analysis that no existing tool performs. G-NEW-3 (within-object CC extraction) is documented but not enforced by scan scripts.
critical_gaps.recommendation: Implement G-NEW automated checks: (1) topic-relevance scoring for EW fields, (2) within-object CC extraction mandate in all scan tools, (3) case explanation depth validator for G-NEW-4.

critical_gaps.title: Template Rotation — Persistent Source of Multiple Defect Classes
critical_gaps.description: The 5-item template rotation engine is the root cause of DL-008, DL-010, DL-016, DL-026, DL-012, DL-015, and DL-031. Seven distinct defect classes trace to a single authoring pattern: items generated in 5-item groups with rotational CC assignments and positional field population. This is a design-level defect in the content authoring pipeline, not a per-item defect.
sources: DEFECT_LIBRARY.md DL-008, DL-010, DL-012, DL-015, DL-016, DL-026, DL-031
critical_gaps.recommendation: Deprecate the rotation template engine. If new items are authored, use a single-item pipeline with per-item field verification. For existing items, remediation must be systematic (fix the rotation group, not individual items in isolation).
